title: THE SEVEN BOWLS
mv: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.
mvp: “Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.” Revelation 15:1 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention what you will do to avoid being part of the great tribulation (No mark).

b.x: The seven bowls (or vial) judgements represent the final outpouring of God's wrath during the tribulation period. These will be the most intense and devastating judgements the world has ever experienced. Described in Revelation 16:1-21, they are referred to specifically as “the seven bowls of God’s wrath.” At this point in history, human wickedness, especially under the reign of the Antichrist, has reached its peak, provoking God's righteous judgement. These seven bowl judgements are initiated following the sounding of the seventh trumpet.

The First Bowl: The first angel pours his bowl onto the land, and painful, festering sores break out on those who bear the mark of the beast and worship its image (Revelation 16:2). This judgement specifically targets followers of the Antichrist. Believers faithful to Christ during the tribulation period are not affected.

The Second Bowl: The second angel pours his bowl into the sea, turning it into blood, “like that of a dead person,” causing every living creature in the sea to die (Revelation 16:3). The devastation is total; the oceans are lifeless.
The Third Bowl: With the third bowl, God’s wrath is poured out on rivers and springs, turning all freshwater sources into blood (Revelation 16:4-5).

The Fourth Bowl: The fourth angel pours his bowl on the sun, and its heat intensifies, scorching people with fire (Revelation 16:8-9). Instead of repenting, the people curse God's name, even though they know He is behind the plagues.

The Fifth Bowl: The fifth bowl plunges the Antichrist’s kingdom into darkness. The suffering becomes so severe that people chew their tongues in agony (Revelation 16:10-11). Despite this pain, they remain unrepentant and continue to defy God.

The Sixth Bowl: The sixth angel pours out his bowl on river Euphrates, drying it up to prepare the way for the kings of the East (Revelation 16:12). John sees three unclean spirits (demonic forces resembling frogs), emerge from the mouth of Satan, the Antichrist, and the false prophet (Revelation 16:13). These spirits perform miraculous signs to deceive the kings of the world and gather them for the final battle on the Day of the Lord (Revelation 16:14). They assemble at a place called “Armageddon” (Revelation 16:16).

The Seventh Bowl: The seventh bowl is poured into the atmosphere, and a loud voice from heaven declares, “It is done” (Revelation 16:17). This is followed by lightning, thunder, and a massive earthquake; greater than any the world has ever seen (Revelation 16:18). Jerusalem is split into three parts, global cities collapse, islands sink, and mountains vanish (Revelation 16:19-20). Huge hailstones, each weighing about 100 pounds (45.36kg), fall from the sky (Revelation 16:21). Yet even after all this, people continue to curse God because of the severity of the judgement.

The bowl judgements lead directly to the defeats of the forces of the Antichrist at the “Battle of Armageddon” and Jesus' return in power and glory (Revelation 19:11-21) to establish His “millennial kingdom,” a thousand-year reign of peace and righteousness (Revelation 20:1-6). The bowl judgements:

i: Signal the end of human rebellion and the final confrontation between good and evil.
Lack partiality (like the trumpet or seal judgements); they are total, swift, and irreversible (Revelation 15:1).

Reflect God's justice, as they are poured out on those who worship the beast, blaspheme God, and refuse to repent. Even the angels declare God’s judgements as “true and righteous” (Revelation 16:5-7).

b.x: Together, the seals, trumpets, and bowls of the end times comprise “the great day of God’s wrath” (Revelation 6:17) and serve to judge the Antichrist’s kingdom of wickedness.

i: What do you understand by the “seven bowls?”
Mention three important aspects of the seven bowl judgement.
